notes: The Park Commissioners' reports bound into the pre-1906 Municipal Reports (FY1869-70 to FY1906-07), read in full for dated facts about named park structures, lakes, gardens and squares; plus the 1870 parks act (vol for 1869-70, Supplement LXXI), the Dewey Monument committee's report (1902-03, pp. 1105-1113) and the Board of Health's report on the Park Emergency Hospital (1901-02). Read by five parallel readers, one per span of volumes; every quote re-checked against the OCR.

coverage.remaining: The rest of every pre-1906 volume: the Superintendent of Schools' and Fire Department reports (schools and firehouses, located by block face in pre-1909 numbering), the Board of Public Works and the City Hall commissioners. FY1860-61 and FY1895-96 (only the excerpts volume) are not on the Internet Archive in full.
coverage.note: 47 volumes, FY1859-60 to FY1906-07; 37 carry park material (none before the April 1870 act). 393 facts: 232 placed on a place page or the park parcel, 91 published as 88 timeline entries on 39 pages, 141 declined as minor, retrospective or already on the page; 161 unresolved for want of a page (drives, walks, nursery and utility buildings, and demolished structures: the Casino, the aviary, the first music stand). From 1893-94 most volumes print only accounts, so those facts are ledger lines dated to the fiscal year.
